fallback.text: A Bloom filter of m = 1000 bits holding n = 100 items. With k hash functions a lookup of an item that was never stored still says yes when all k of its bits are set, which happens with probability about (1 − e^(−kn/m))^k. One hash gives 9.5 %, three give 1.7 %, and the best number, k = (m/n)·ln 2 ≈ 6.9, rounded to 7, gives 0.82 %. More hashes than that fill the filter faster than they help. The exact rate, from the law of the number of set bits, is 0.83 % (Christensen, Roginsky and Jimeno, 2010).
